definiteTranslationRepairs.before: In the first year of Taishi under Emperor Ming, he was transferred to Left Army Staff Officer of the Ministry of Rites, General Who Conquers, and Governor of Southern Donghai.
definiteTranslationRepairs.after: In the first year of Taishi under Emperor Ming, he was transferred to Left Chief Clerk to the Minister of Education (Situ), Champion General, and Governor of Southern Donghai.
definiteTranslationRepairs.reason: 司徒 is Situ (Minister of Education), not the Ministry of Rites; 冠軍將軍 is Champion General.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 轉司徒左長史，冠軍將軍

definiteTranslationRepairs.before: When affairs were settled, he was made Supervisor of the Secretariat, with his original title as Commissioner with the Golden Grandee's insignia and ceremonial staff equal to the Three Dukes, heading the Ministry of Rites; Yang Province was dissolved as his headquarters—he firmly refused to move.
definiteTranslationRepairs.after: When affairs were settled, he was made Supervisor of the Secretariat, with his original title as Commissioner with ceremonial staff equal to the Three Dukes, heading the Minister of Education (Situ) post; the Yang Province headquarters building was assigned as his office—he firmly refused to move.
definiteTranslationRepairs.reason: 領司徒 means heading the Situ post, not Ministry of Rites; 以揚州解為府 means using the Yang Province office as his headquarters.

definiteTranslationRepairs.before: When Emperor Shun took the throne, he was moved to Supervisor of the Secretariat, with his posts as Minister of Rites and Palace Attendant unchanged.
definiteTranslationRepairs.after: When Emperor Shun took the throne, he was moved to Supervisor of the Secretariat, with his posts as Minister of Education (Situ) and Palace Attendant unchanged.
definiteTranslationRepairs.reason: 司徒 is Situ, not Minister of Rites.
